subject: Customer-keystore: onshore custody, subprocessor routing & DPA clarifications
messages:
From: Sarah Warden <sarah.warden@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA + private deploy questions (keystore custody, subprocessors, onshore routing)

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start mapping procurement with our InfoSec and Legal teams, two priority topics came up around private deployments: keystore custody (we need to understand operator access and whether we can hold the root key), and the list + routing of subprocessors for on-prem/VPC deployments (particularly any cross-border egress paths).

Can you share an updated DPA that reflects:
- Customer-held key options (KMS/HSM integration, offline escrow alternatives)
- Clear demarcation of Redwood operator access and break-glass procedures
- A subprocessors matrix with onshore-only processing options and routing guarantees (if available)

If possible, please send an annotated draft we can circulate to our procurement and security teams. We are targeting an internal review by 03/25.

—Sarah
Sarah Warden
Director, Procurement — Acme Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Warden <sarah.warden@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA + private deploy questions (keystore custody, subprocessors, onshore routing)

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. They want an annotated DPA and a subprocessors matrix that supports an onshore-only option for private deployment. Key points: customer-held keys (they may insist on exclusive custody), break-glass/operator access clarity, and explicit routing constraints for subprocessors.

Quick thoughts:
- We have a customer-managed KMS flow (customer holds root KEK) for Private; need to confirm HSM pairing & managed-escrow language.
- Operator access is already limited by role & audit; but Legal wants explicit paragraph on break-glass approvals and audit trail retention.
- Subprocessor routing: we can guarantee region-based processing for Private if they commit to dedicated capacity in a given region; must call out exceptions for managed updates/bugfixing windows where specialists may need temporary access under NDA.

Kimberly, can you draft the annotated DPA language (high level) and push redlines? Karthik/Marissa — can you produce a concise subprocessors_onshore_matrix and a short diagram for the handshake flow (customer KMS -> Redwood runtime -> operator interventions)? I will coordinate a consolidated response to Acme and attach the DPA redline.

Thanks, Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Warden <sarah.warden@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2029 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA + private deploy questions (keystore custody, subprocessors, onshore routing)

Mina / team — attaching the first-pass annotated DPA (attached as DPA_Acme_v2_redlines.docx). Key callouts I added:

1) Customer Key Custody: clause that allows customer to provide KEK via their KMS endpoint (we never persist root key). Includes an escrow path: customer may opt into an encrypted key-escrow vault accessible only under multi-party legal/technical approval (we defined a 3-person approval set).

2) Operator Access / Break-Glass: explicit "approval-only" break-glass procedure for production tenant access; actions are timeboxed, fully logged, and require post-access attestation. I added timing SLAs for access requests (response within 4 business hours for critical incidents).

3) Subprocessors & Routing: included a table requirement that Redwood will only route inference traffic to onshore subprocessors when customer has selected the "onshore-only" private deployment option and has procured a regional capacity reservation. Also included an exception carve-out for emergency troubleshooting visits by named teams (SRE/security) with prior customer approval.

Open items where I need input:
- Precise wording for the escrow-holder model (legal will want more granularity on custody and revocation).
- Whether Acme requires irrevocable denial of operator decryption (we'd need to confirm feasibility for support/debug).

Attaching redlines and will update once Karthik confirms the handshake diagram.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_Acme_v2_redlines.docx (redlines, comments inline)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Warden <sarah.warden@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 20 Mar 2029 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA + private deploy questions (keystore custody, subprocessors, onshore routing)

Mina / Kim — attached is the subprocessors_onshore_matrix.csv and a short keystore_handshake_diagram.png (summarized below). High-level technical demarcation:

- Customer KMS integration: customer provides a KMS endpoint + public-wrapped KEK. At runtime, Redwood's inference nodes fetch wrapped tokens, unwrap locally in a sealed enclave or HSM-backed module, and use ephemeral DEKs that never leave node memory. Persistent storage of DEKs is not supported.

- Operator access: operators can request ephemeral session keys via the break-glass flow only; those sessions generate an immutable audit entry and are time-limited (default 1 hour). All operator sessions require a 2-party approval from Redwood's on-call security and the customer's appointed approver (we support both direct API approval and signed DocuSign confirmations for emergency access).

- Onshore routing: subprocessors listed in the attached matrix are only used for data plane processing when the customer selects the dedicated onshore private deployment option and the deployment is pinned to that region. For hybrid maintenance (patching, update rollout), we propose a temporary, pre-approved maintenance window and a simple notice + approval workflow.

Caveats: cross-border diagnostic support (if requested by customer) will be explicitly logged and should be subject to an additional scoping attachment to the DPA.

-Karthik
Engineering Lead, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessors_onshore_matrix.csv, keystore_handshake_diagram.png

Date: Thu, 21 Mar 2029 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + private deploy questions (keystore custody, subprocessors, onshore routing)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached are the annotated DPA redlines, a subprocessors onshore matrix that enumerates which managed services and support teams are region-bound, and a one-page handshake diagram that shows customer KMS -> runtime key unwrap -> ephemeral DEK lifecycle.

Summary of what we can commit to in the DPA draft:
- Customer-controlled KEK: we will include the customer-managed KMS option (no root key persistence) and an optional encrypted-escrow mechanism under a multi-party approval process.
- Operator break-glass: access is approval-gated, time-limited, auditable, and requires customer-appointed approval in normal and emergency paths.
- Onshore-only subprocessors: available as a deployment option and enforced when customer reserves regional capacity; exceptions (emergency debug, urgent patching) are covered under a documented temporary access process and require pre-approval or post-notice depending on the case.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached DPA_Acme_v2_redlines.docx and flag any specific language you want tightened (escrow holder, irrevocable access denial, or SLA expectations).
2) If the onshore-only routing model is acceptable, we'll convert the subprocessors_onshore_matrix into an annex to the DPA and add the operational maintenance workflow as an exhibit.
3) We can arrange a short working session next week with Karthik and our SRE lead to walk Acme's security team through the handshake diagram.

If you'd like, we can also include a signature-ready DPA + annex once we agree the escrow and access wording. Targeting to get a draft for your procurement by 03/25 if we have your comments by Monday 03/25 12pm PT.

Regards,
Mina
Head of Trust & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Acme_v2_redlines.docx; subprocessors_onshore_matrix.csv; keystore_handshake_diagram.png
